To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DNNs are a promising approach for SC but not for AED.

DNNs and TDNNs can be successfully applied for SC and AED tasks, but for the AED task the performance of DNN-based systems is not yet comparable with the performance of the best traditional systems, and the performance of DMM-based systems is still superior for the AED problem.
DNN-based SC systems outperform the DCASE'2016 baseline system, and that DNNs are not the best choice for AED, but can still be useful for feature extraction and for the back end of HMMs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the best neural network NN architecture for acoustic scene classification and acoustic event detection?
the following three main topics: 1 The use of DNNs for SC and AED, 2 The use of TDNNs for SC, 3 The use of GFB features for SC and ADE.
the question how to design and train neural networks for SC and AED.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for both tasks DNNs are not yet the state-of-the-art.
DNNs are not the ultimate solution for all problems in audio scene analysis, but they provide valuable tools to improve existing systems.
DNN-based SC systems are competitive to traditional approaches, while for AED DNNs do not seem to be the best choice for the task at hand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNNs are not the best solution for the SC task and that DNNs do not perform as well as GFBs for the AED task.
the use of deep NNs in SC systems is promising but that further research is required to fully exploit the benefits of these architectures for AED systems.
DNN-based approaches can outperform GMM-based systems for SC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for SC, DNNs with GFB features are the best performing system.
DNNs are a powerful tool for SC but are less suitable for AED in the context of the DCASE 2013 and 2016 challenges.
the use of DNNs and GFBs for SC and AED is promising, and that there are still open questions regarding the design of DNN-based systems and the feature extraction process.
